cause: **Searching for the grader instead of the spec.** Steps go to git history, tags, remotes, and test-file globs in hopes of finding hidden tests. It should read the visible tests once for interface, and spend the rest on SPEC.md.
subject: Prompt: read spec, tests once, skip hidden-test hunting.
description: I added one bullet to the "How to work" list in `src/prompt.ts` (the stable system prefix, so it costs nothing extra per request): it tells jig to work from the task as written, read the task's specification, read any tests the task comes with just once for the interface they pin down, and not hunt for the hidden tests that grade it. This targets the observed failure directly: instead of spending steps on git history, tags, remotes and test-file globs looking for a grader it cannot find, jig is steered to the spec and the visible interface, which should cut wasted steps (cost) while keeping attention on what the task actually requires. The full suite shows only the 7 pre-existing sandbox failures and no new ones.

verdict.reason: no better on the training tasks (+7 points, ahead in 53% of resamples, cost ×0.99)
